newsitem.title: USA: Clinton begins inaugural with prayer service.
newsitem.headline: Clinton begins inaugural with prayer service.

text.p: Symbolising his hopes for national harmony, President Bill Clinton on Monday started his second inaugural in prayer at a predominantly black church less than a mile (1.6 km) from the White House.

Accompanied by his wife Hillary and daughter Chelsea, Clinton arrived at the Metropolitan AME Church shortly after 8 a.m. EST (1200 GMT) to join Vice President Al Gore and his family for a joyous inter-faith religious service.

Clinton, in a dark business suit and spurning a topcoat, shook hands with a clergyman and several bystanders as he entered the red brick church where he also worshipped at the start of his first inaugural in 1993. Mrs. Clinton wore a tailored peach-coloured suit without a hat.
The prayer service was the first official event on a day of ceremony and celebration that will last into the early hours of Tuesday morning.
Clinton was to be sworn in for a second four-year term in the White House at a noon ceremony at the U.S. Capitol.
He then was to sketch out his vision for the United States as it enters the 21st century in a speech expected to place heavy emphasis on the need for political reconciliation.
